newsitem.title: FRANCE: French unemployment hits record 12.6 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: French unemployment hits record 12.6 pct in Sept.

text.p: French jobless numbers leapt by 27,700 in September to set a record unemployment rate of 12.6 percent, figures issued by the labour ministry showed.

The rise in the seasonally adjusted number of people unemployed, up 0.9 percent from August, was larger than expected, taking the total number out of work to 3,112,800 from 3,085,100, the Labour Ministry said on Thursday.
The jobless rate, based on International Labour Organisation (ILO) criteria, which exclude jobseekers who did any work, was up at a record 12.6 percent from a revised 12.5 percent in August.
Economists said the figures were gloomy news.
"It's really crystal clear, this is really bad," said Valerie Plagnol, economist at French bank Credit Commercial de France.
Joanne Perez, a strategist at Merrill Lynch in Paris, said: "I think in order for this to pass the Bank of France will have to cut rates as a sweetener, it's bad enough for a cut."

"What's interesting is that we've had a big pick up in part-time employment in recent months. The unemployed plus the under-unemployed is something more like 3.23 million which puts the rate nearer to 13 percent.
"It suggests the consumer side of the economy is going to remain weak for some time."
